findings.description: The long-context threshold checks only input_tokens, although cached input is supplied separately as cache_read_tokens and cache_creation_tokens.
findings.failure_mode: A request with 10,000 uncached input tokens and 250,000 cache-read tokens bypasses a 200,000-token threshold. All input, cache, and output costs are then recorded without the premium, understating ledger spend and budget consumption.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare the threshold against total input tokens, including cache reads and cache creation, while preserving separate rates for each category.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: The context-budget shrink consumes an iteration of the existing retry loop without ensuring another iteration remains.
findings.failure_mode: With max_retries=0, a recoverable input-plus-output context error replaces the request and executes continue, but the loop immediately ends without submitting the smaller request. The same failure occurs when the context error arrives on the final attempt after other transient failures. This also bypasses propagation of the provider context verdict to the calibration handler.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the single context shrink its own retry allowance, or explicitly retry the reduced request independently of the transient retry counter. Preserve ProviderContextLimitError if recovery cannot run.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: The one-shot output-budget shrink is implemented as `request = replace(request, max_tokens=room); continue` inside the `for attempt in range(max_retries + 1)` loop, and `last_typed_error` is never set to the ProviderContextLimitError. When the context-limit error arrives on the final iteration (always, when `retry.max_retries` is 0; otherwise whenever earlier attempts were consumed by 429/503 backoff), `continue` exits the loop and the shrunk request is never sent. Control falls through to the post-loop exhausted path, which does not carry a ProviderContextLimitError, so cheval's new `except ProviderContextLimitError` in cmd_invoke never fires.
findings.failure_mode: Under max_retries=0 (or a late context-limit error) the provider's size verdict is converted into the generic exhausted error: cheval treats it as walkable, sends the identical oversize payload to the next chain voice (the exact outcome D-1.1b forbids), no observed-bound row is recorded, and the exit is CHAIN_EXHAUSTED/typed-as-outage rather than CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE with calibration_needed.
findings.suggested_fix: Set `last_typed_error = e` before the shrink path, and either perform the shrunk retry outside the attempt counter (e.g. a `while True` wrapper or `attempt -= 1` equivalent) or, when `attempt == max_retries`, re-raise `e` instead of `continue`. Add a test with max_retries=0 asserting ProviderContextLimitError propagates.

findings.cross_file_justification: The new 16K non-Anthropic default feeds `_hop_max_tokens` in cheval.py; the walk-loop I1 fit (cheval.py:2078-2086) explicitly skips entries without `effective_input_ceiling`/`probed_ceiling`, i.e. every OpenAI/Google/xAI hop, so the only check left for those hops is the adapter's own `enforce_context_window`.
findings.description: Non-Anthropic hops jump from a 4,096 default output budget to min(16,000, catalog max_output_tokens), but the per-hop I1 shrink only applies to entries carrying an HTTP input ceiling (Anthropic). For a gpt-*/gemini-* fallback hop the budget is therefore never fitted to the window, and the adapter's `enforce_context_window` evaluates input + max_tokens with a budget 4x larger than before.
findings.failure_mode: Inputs that previously fit a non-Anthropic fallback (estimate within 4K..16K of the window, e.g. ~115K on a 128K entry) now raise ContextTooLargeError inside the adapter and walk/exhaust the chain. The regression is silent: the walk-gate threshold for these entries did not change, so the operator sees a ROUTING_MISS/CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE that did not occur before the cycle.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the I1 fit to every hop that declares `context_window` (drop the ceiling-field condition, or gate on `context_window` only), or have `enforce_context_window` shrink max_tokens to the floor before raising, mirroring `_fit_max_tokens`.

findings.cross_file_justification: `_walk_estimate` is overwritten with the provider's count_tokens value (anthropic_adapter.count_tokens, new in this diff) and then drives `_fit_max_tokens` in the walk loop; the adapter's `enforce_context_window` re-derives the input size from the chars/3.5 heuristic, so the two checks use different numbers for the same request.
findings.description: When the pre-flight counter runs, the authoritative provider count replaces the heuristic in `_walk_estimate` and the I1 fit grants `max_tokens = context_window - count`. The adapter's `enforce_context_window` still uses `estimate_tokens(messages)`. For prose where chars/3.5 overcounts Claude tokens (English runs ~4 chars/token), count < heuristic, so the fit grants a budget the adapter then rejects (heuristic + fitted max_tokens > context_window).
findings.failure_mode: A request the provider itself says fits (and that the pre-flight gate approved with 'warn'/'dispatch') is refused by the adapter with ContextTooLargeError and walked to the next voice, or exhausts the chain. The envelope reports a count-based estimate while the failure message cites the heuristic, which is confusing to debug.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the authoritative estimate into the request (e.g. CompletionRequest.metadata['input_tokens_counted']) and let `enforce_context_window` prefer it, or compute the fit from the same `estimate_tokens(messages)` value the adapter will use and keep the count only for the bound comparison.

findings.description: The long-context tier triggers on `input_tokens > threshold` only. Per ledger.create_ledger_entry's own contract, `cache_read_tokens` / `cache_creation_tokens` are 'not part of input_tokens'. Anthropic's 1M-window premium is assessed on the total prompt size including cached prefix, so a request with 150K cached + 100K fresh tokens (250K total) is billed at the premium by the provider but recorded at base rates here.
findings.failure_mode: Systematic under-reporting of cost in the ledger and cost-report for prompt-cached long-context runs (exactly the workload flatline/bridgebuilder produce), while `long_context: true` is absent so the rows are not even counted as premium rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate the threshold against `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens`; add a unit test with cached tokens straddling the threshold.

findings.description: The new probe only falls back to a one-token message when GET /models returns exactly 404. Any other non-200 (403/405/501 from gateways that only route /messages, 400 from strict proxies, or a 5xx envelope from a proxy that drops unknown paths) returns False without trying the message probe that previously defined health. The docstring's own premise ('only when the endpoint is not served (404, a proxy)') is narrower than real proxy behaviour.
findings.failure_mode: loa-status / provider health reports a healthy proxied Anthropic deployment as down after this change, a regression from the pre-cycle behaviour where the message probe alone decided health.
findings.suggested_fix: Fall back to the tiny-model message probe on any non-200 that is not an auth failure (401/403 with an Anthropic error body), or on every non-200, and only return False when the message probe also fails.

findings.description: The stderr notice that an explicit operator `--max-tokens` was shrunk by I1 is in an `elif` behind `action == "warn"`, so a request that is both above the probed bound (warn) and shrunk prints only the warn line. In the walk loop, fallback-hop shrinks (cheval.py:2098-2103) write only to the envelope with no stderr line at all. The reviewer asked specifically where an explicit `--max-tokens` is changed silently; these are the two places.
findings.failure_mode: An operator who passed `--max-tokens 64000` gets a shorter completion (possibly truncated at the 4,096 floor) with no operator-visible indication other than the MODELINV envelope field.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit the shrink notice independently of the warn branch (two `if`s, not `if/elif`), and print the same `[preflight] max_tokens shrunk` line in the walk loop when `_fit.shrunk_from` is set and `_explicit_max_tokens` was given.
